report.source_text: A non-contrast brain CT scan revealed a chronic subdural hematoma, Markwalder grade 2, located on the left hemisphere, at the level of frontal and parietal lobes, depicting a hypodense aspect measuring about 1.5 cm, without mass effect or subfalcine herniation. Moderate age-related cerebral abiotrophy was also observed (Figure 1).

report.source_text: At discharge, the patient showed slightly remitted right hemiparesis MRC 4/5; regarding Gerstmann syndrome presentation, no improvements or worsening of the symptoms was observed, and she was prescribed Fludrocortisone for the intracranial hematoma.

clinician.final_diagnosis: an 86-year-old patient, who exhibited all the hallmark symptoms of Gerstmann syndrome, and additionally, an atypical presentation of Gerstmann syndrome in the context of a chronic subdural hematoma
clinician.trajectory_summary: An 86-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with a three-week history of right-sided hemiparesis and cognitive signs consistent with Gerstmann syndrome (finger agnosia, agraphia, acalculia, right-left disorientation). Neurological examination confirmed these findings. A non-contrast head CT on admission demonstrated a left frontal-parietal chronic subdural hematoma, Markwalder grade 2, without mass effect. Follow-up CT the next day showed signs of hematoma resorption. At discharge, the patient displayed mild improvement in right hemiparesis (MRC 4/5), but Gerstmann syndrome features persisted unchanged. The patient was treated conservatively with Fludrocortisone.
